for_paul_decision.title: Firstport Start It Programme — LIVE ROW, needs your call
for_paul_decision.quote: Who's it for? Individuals with a business idea that addresses a social, environmental and/or community issue. ... Eligibility To apply for Start It, you must meet the following eligibility criteria: You are aged 18 or over. You are a permanent resident of Scotland.
for_paul_decision.note: The brief said to relink this row to Start It's own page and correct its fields. Reading that page changes the question. Start It is individuals only, which under CLAUDE.md's audience rule makes the row out_of_scope, so the right action is a reject rather than a more precise link, and that is a live row during the launch freeze so it is yours not mine. Three further mismatches against the page, all on a LIVE row: it holds £5,000 to £25,000 where the page says 'Up to £5,000' and £25,000 appears nowhere on it; it lists seven eligible_structures (CICs, charities, SCIOs, co-ops, ltd) where the page's only tests are a person's age and residence; and its description calls it a programme for 'social entrepreneurs and early-stage social enterprises'. Its apply_url is also still the funding index. Not touched by this job.

report.title: UnLtd Awards
report.quote: You must be 16 years old or over . View full eligibility criteria
report.note: Has a genuine named intake ("Next round on 1 October 2026 at 10:00") and real awards up to £18,000 with support attached, so it fails only the third test. The award goes to the social entrepreneur: the eligibility tests are a person's age and right to live and work in the UK, and incorporation is optional ("If you have already incorporated your social venture, it must be registered in the UK").

report.title: Pilotlight Weston Charity Awards
report.city: North of England, Midlands and Wales
report.quote: Twenty-two charities from the North of England, the Midlands and Wales have been named as winners of the 2026 Weston Charity Awards. Each charity will receive a support package worth over £22,000, incl
report.note: Held twice: 73c320f7 (archived, same URL as this) and adc7ec22 (between_rounds_scheduled, on garfieldweston.org). Pilotlight is thoroughly covered besides, with Pilotlight 360 (c1caaf02) and Pro Bono Support Matching (c1a86516) both LIVE. Worth Paul knowing the 2026 winners are announced and the awards run annually, so between_rounds_scheduled on adc7ec22 looks like the correct state.

report.title: Key Fund
report.city: North of England and the Midlands
report.quote: We can provide investments from £5k to £300k to community and social enterprises.
report.note: Thirteen Key Fund rows in the table, including 'Key Fund Flexible Finance' LIVE at exactly the URL read here, plus Property Fund, Community Business Fund, Northern Impact Fund 2, Northern Cultural Regeneration Fund and More than a Pub all live. This provider is comprehensively covered.

report.title: Big Issue Invest
report.quote: We invest in social enterprises and charities, creating core solutions to end poverty and inequality in the UK.
report.note: Held as 124a6b30 (archived) and d1fa687c (rejected), plus Power Up London separately. Both existing rows are hidden, so if Paul wants Big Issue Invest live it is an un-reject rather than a new row.

report.title: Plunkett UK
report.quote: Plunkett UK is a national charity supporting rural community businesses across the UK. We provide specialist business advice at every stage of the journey – from the initial idea and start-up, to long after opening.
report.note: Membership plus specialist business advice and training. No named intake and nothing awarded, so it is the class Paul ruled out, not a cohort.

report.title: Impact Hub (global network site)
report.quote: We connect entrepreneurs and innovators to large organisations, partners, investors, and the public sector.
report.note: The global .net site is a membership network (Impact Maker Membership) rather than a programme with an intake. Impact Hub London is separately held already (between_rounds_scheduled). Individual UK Impact Hub locations run their own accelerators and would need checking location by location, which is a provider-level job rather than one row.
